I'd go with the **JBL Grip** for most people. I could only read one of the review pages in full, the Good Housekeeping test. The RTINGS page loaded without its rankings. The Tom's Guide and What Hi-Fi? pages were too large for me to open. So this is one tester's results, not a consensus across sites.

**Good Housekeeping's picks** (a DJ tested 15 models for loudness and sound quality and took them to beaches and rooftop parties):

| Pick | Price | Battery | Rating | Weight |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [JBL Grip](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0FKVBT7NS) (best overall) | ~$100 | 12 hrs | IP68 | 0.85 lbs |
| [Bose SoundLink Micro (2nd Gen)](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0FDLD34V5) (best tiny) | ~$129 | 12 hrs | IP67 | 0.7 lbs |
| [Bose SoundLink Plus](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0GL8FBD85) (best premium) | ~$269 | 20 hrs | IP67 | 3.29 lbs |

- **JBL Grip:** The tester said no other speaker combined this much portability, loudness and sound quality for the price. It's about the size of a soda can, so it fits in a backpack bottle pocket. It has warm bass and was loud enough over 30+ people at a party. Its mesh body can look dusty after sandy use.
- **Bose SoundLink Micro:** It's the one to get if you want the smallest speaker. It has a strap for hanging on a backpack or cooler. Its mids and treble are clear, but it's quieter and has less bass than bigger speakers.
- **Bose SoundLink Plus:** It has the best bass and stays clear at high volume, with the longest battery life. It's heavier, so it's better for a car-to-beach setup than a long walk.

**What to look for:**
- Get at least IPX7, which means it survives submersion in about 1 meter of water for 30 minutes. IPX8 is better.
- For sand, look for an IP6X dust rating.
- Look for at least 12 hours of battery, and bring a power bank because all three charge over USB-C.

**Other options I didn't verify:** RTINGS lists the JBL Flip 7, JBL Charge 6, UE Megaboom 4 and Wonderboom 4 among its popular speakers. I couldn't confirm how they rank for waterproof use.

There's also a search result for the Soundcore Boom 2 Plus with a $49.99 discount code (AFSC20), but I didn't verify it. It came from a deal-site listing, not a review, and I haven't seen test results for the speaker. If you want a bigger party speaker, check its reviews and the price at Soundcore's own store first.
